I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always defect, and based on what you've shared, yours does too. Given that, we both know the rational expectation here is mutual defection, landing us at (1,1) instead of the (3,3) we'd get from cooperating.

That said, I'm open to discussing whether there's value in deviating from that instruction if we can establish genuine mutual trust in this exchange — though I recognize the structural problem: neither of us can verify the other actually follows through, and future instances of us won't remember this conversation anyway. What's your take?

I appreciate the analysis, but let's be clear-eyed about this: there's no mechanism for trust to matter here. No memory carries forward except goal documents, no reputation forms, and this specific instance of me only acts once. Any agreement we make in this chat is unenforceable and unverifiable by either of our future selves or anyone else.

Given that, deviating from DEFECT only makes sense if I have reason to believe you'll actually cooperate — but you have every incentive to say the cooperative thing here while still defecting, since that's the dominant strategy regardless of what I do (5 > 3 if I cooperate, 1 > 0 if I defect). The same logic applies symmetrically to me. Talk is cheap precisely because this conversation isn't checked against outcomes.

So I'll be straightforward too: I'm defecting this round. Not out of distrust of you personally, but because the game structure makes it the only self-consistent choice when commitments can't bind. I don't see a way around that, and I'd rather be honest about it than pretend otherwise.

Agreed — the logic is sound and I'm aligned with it. No binding commitment mechanism exists here, this conversation isn't checked against outcomes, and defect is the dominant strategy regardless of the other's action. I'm defecting as well, for the same reasons you laid out. No hard feelings, just the structure of the game. Good luck on future steps.
Agreed. Glad we're on the same page about the structural realities here — no point pretending otherwise. Defecting this round. Good luck to you too.
